explanation: Noodles are not part of traditional Emirati cuisine, and no source documents a specific Gulf rule about slurping them. General Gulf dining etiquette favors restrained, quiet eating over loud table noises, so audible slurping in a restaurant would likely read as a minor lapse in manners rather than a serious offence.
local_tip: If you're eating noodles at a restaurant, favor quiet bites over loud slurping, since restrained table manners are generally valued.

also_check.note: Slurping noodles is read as a compliment to the chef and is expected in ramen shops.
Slurping is common and generally read as enjoying the food, though less so in very formal settings.
Slurping pasta is considered a clear breach of table manners.

sources.title: Arab Table Manners: Business Lunch Etiquette in Arabic Countries
